about: Lessons from a private training lab, cleared for shipping: measured findings and sourced conventions. Not rules, and not listening results unless a lesson says so.

lessons.concept: Drill 808: holds the root, glides as a pickup, tuned
lessons.interpretation: The 808 holds the root, one or two notes a bar, and glides as a pickup into the next bar; slides are what make UK drill. An out-of-tune 808 alone makes a beat sound amateur.
lessons.technique: Tune the 808 to the key (check its pitch in cents), one or two notes a bar, glide into the downbeat.
lessons.limitations: Secondary sources; slide density varies by producer.
lessons.sources: Native Instruments blog; Complex (M1OnTheBeat interview); 808Melo quoted via Genius; FADER (Mike Dean, '808 on the wrong note')

lessons.interpretation: About 138-145 BPM felt half time. Snare or clap on beat 3, often moving over two bars (beat 3 of bar 1, beat 4 of bar 2) with ghost snares at phrase ends. Hats grouped (3+3+2) with stepped velocities and deliberate holes, straight 16ths mixed with triplet bursts, varied over a 4-bar phrase.
lessons.technique: Program the snare over two bars, group the hats with holes, vary the pattern every 4 bars.
lessons.limitations: Secondary sources and producer statements; conventions vary by scene and era; not a target to enforce.
lessons.sources: Native Instruments blog 'drill'; Attack Magazine 'Beat dissected: UK drill'; Tracklib (808Melo, Dior); Amped Studio; DJ Mag 'Evolving sound of UK drill'

lessons.concept: Notes are not sound: Live's '808 Pure' rings on after note-off, so shorter MIDI notes open no low-end space
lessons.interpretation: The preset's release outlasts every gap the shorter notes leave, so the 808 never stops. The offline lab assumed note-off means silence; for this instrument that is false.
lessons.technique: Before using note length to make space, measure the instrument: play a short note and read its level 100-250 ms after note-off. If it rings on, shorten the amp release (or use a gate) and measure again.
lessons.faderhand_guidance: Run preflight.py set on the saved Set and preflight.py occupancy on the stems inside planned gaps; read the 808's release with get_device_parameters before relying on note length.
lessons.limitations: One preset; measured, not heard. Other 808 presets (Sampler in Trigger mode, short-release synths) differ.

observations.level_change_250ms_after_note_off_db: within -1.7..+1.2 of the note's peak at 50% length

lessons.basis: Measured on controlled renders with known causes (offline and/or in Ableton Live). Not a listening result unless it says so.

lessons.concept: Shortening the 808 opens the low register but does not clear the kick
lessons.interpretation: Gating the 808 to half its length took the low end from sounding 82% of the time to 55% and created about two low-register gaps a bar, but the kick stayed about 6.3 dB under the 808 at the hit: the overlap is at the 808 start, not its tail.
lessons.technique: Two tools for two problems: gate the 808 for space in the low register, duck it (sidechain) for kick clarity. Gating by note length works only if the 808 releases at note-off: check the instrument first (see the 808 Pure lesson), and shorten its amp release or use a gate if it rings on.
lessons.limitations: Offline synth 808 and kick; measured, not heard. In Live with the Core Library '808 Pure' the same note lengths changed nothing: the low end sounded 100% of the time at every length.
lessons.basis: Measured on controlled renders with known causes (offline and/or in Ableton Live). Not a listening result unless it says so.

lessons.concept: Thinning closed hats creates measurable negative space
lessons.interpretation: Halving the hats moved the empty-16th share from 44% to 61%; quartering it to 72%. It also removed most of the mix's air band, so space in the rhythm costs brightness unless something else carries the top.
lessons.technique: For space without losing the top end: thin the hats but keep one bright element (an open hat, a shaker on the offbeat) or group the hats (3+3+2) rather than deleting evenly.
lessons.faderhand_guidance: Edit the hat clip (create_arrangement_midi_clip with fewer notes) or mute a hat layer; count the empty 16th slots in the drum stem before and after, and check the top end.
lessons.limitations: Even thinning only; grouped patterns with holes (the drill convention) are not tested yet. Replicated in Live (808 Core Kit): empty 16ths 0.11/0.45/0.58, air 0.12/0.08/0.04%; the kit's hats are darker, so absolute values differ.
lessons.basis: Measured on controlled renders with known causes (offline and/or in Ableton Live). Not a listening result unless it says so.

lessons.concept: How deep to duck an 808 under the kick
lessons.interpretation: Each 3 dB of ducking gave the kick about 1.7 dB against the 808 in the 30 ms after each hit; the mix's sub share and loudness barely moved, because the dip is short.
lessons.technique: Sidechain-compress the 808 from the kick for 6-9 dB of gain reduction, fast attack, release shorter than the gap to the next kick.
lessons.faderhand_guidance: set_sidechain (a Compressor on the 808, sidechained from the kick track) and set_device_parameters; then render, print the kick and 808 as stems, and compare their low bands in the 30 ms after each kick.
lessons.limitations: Synthetic kick and 808, one fixture, measured not heard. The perceptual sweet spot is untested: make a blind pair before treating 6-9 dB as a preference.
lessons.basis: Measured on controlled renders with known causes (offline and/or in Ableton Live). Not a listening result unless it says so.

lessons.concept: Wetness has a ground truth from printed stems, but no mix-only measure detects a short room yet
lessons.interpretation: Stems printed post-mixer in one pass sum to the mix exactly (-143 dB residual with no send), so mix minus stems is the returns' output. The room rose 9 dB for 9 dB of send. In this mix it sat 25-34 dB under the dry signal above 300 Hz, and none of three mix-only measures moved.
lessons.technique: Measure how wet a mix is from printed stems and returns (mix minus the dry stems), not from the mix alone. A mix-only dryness measure is still an open problem: test candidates against this ground truth with longer rooms and sparser parts.
lessons.faderhand_guidance: Print each part post-mixer and the mix in one recording pass; their sum then equals the mix, so the residual isolates the returns. Separate passes do not null: some synths start at a new oscillator phase every time.
lessons.limitations: One short room, one arrangement, quiet sends under a loud 808; measured, not heard. 'Too dry' cannot be checked from a mix yet.

observations.mix_only_candidates: frame floor ratio, onset decay ratio, onset flux: changes within seed noise at every level
